observations.note: The 6-word draft of 2026-09-21 is gone. It lived in the swept drafting tree, predates the --candidate retention mechanism, and no retained-candidates tree exists for this function, so attempt 3 re-derives from assembly. Blueprint recovered: src/func_80216BF4.c is the same code the cartridge inlines for the collision probe here, its InstanceHdr is s32 w[20] which is the 0x50-byte header the frame saves and restores, and src/func_80214624.c supplies the Actor and Plan layouts and is called with (actor, plan, candidate) at three sites.

Attempt 3 first trial: 1036 of 1044 bytes, 177 aligned differing words, first difference at word 26. The whole prologue, both saved-register banks, the 0x2C8 frame and the local layout (a 128-entry candidate array at 0x20, the 0x50-byte header save at 0x220, the desired vector at 0x270) reproduce from: void *candidates[128]; Header saved; Vec3 desired; declared in that order. Nearly all 177 words are the two-word shortfall shifting every later branch offset. The two missing words are the cartridge's redundant null test on the query result after func_8024E7CC, which this draft's optimizer folded away, and a second zero-initialisation of the best pointer in the loop guard's delay slot.

Everything but two words is settled. With a second zero-initialisation of the best pointer before the search loop, the draft is 1040 of 1044 bytes and the structural diff against the cartridge is only: one missing branch on the query result after func_8024E7CC, and the register pairing at the class compare, where the cartridge materialises the constant 1 into s2 and loads the halfword into v0 while the draft does the reverse. Every other instruction of the 261, including the whole search loop, the inlined collision probe and the tail, is identical. Closed by measurement: -fno-thread-jumps, -fno-cse-follow-jumps, -fno-cse-skip-blocks, -fno-expensive-optimizations and -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop all leave 1040 bytes unchanged, and so do a fully nested test chain, a copy of the pointer taken before or after the call, and a goto-threaded merge before the append; the compiler folds the second null test in every one of those. Setting the pointer to null in an else arm does keep the branch but costs four words. The constant must reach a callee-saved register, which means the value is live across a call, so the operand it compares against is a variable that is used again later, not a literal.

The last word is a pass-order fact, not a spelling. Two things must hold at once and this compiler gives only one at a time. Compare the class field against a variable set to one in the block that ends with the liveness branch, and reuse the search loop's own index for it: that variable already crosses calls, so it earns a callee-saved register and the compare comes out as li s2,1 with the halfword in v0, exactly as the cartridge has it. Put the store guard after the block that screens the query result, so its block is a merge: the second null test then survives instead of being folded away. But with jump threading on, the threader redirects the first null test past the store and the merge label dies with it, after which the equivalence one is carried into the store block and the count increment becomes addu s4,s4,s2 instead of addiu s4,s4,1. With -fno-thread-jumps the label lives, the increment is right, and the first null test keeps the near target instead, so that spelling also lands one word out. Measured and ruled out for the increment: -fno-strength-reduce, -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop, -fno-cse-follow-jumps, -fno-expensive-optimizations, -fno-caller-saves, -O3, an unsigned count, a split store and increment, a separate sentinel variable (which fixes the increment but puts the constant in v1 because it crosses no call), a short sentinel, and a redundant forward goto meant to keep the label alive. What is left to try is a third edge into the store guard that the threader cannot resolve, or the permuter.

Re-measured the retained draft artifacts/retained-candidates/func_802149C0/3.c before touching it: 1044 of 1044 bytes, 1 aligned differing word of 261, at word 94 (0x80214B38), expected 26940001 addiu s4,s4,1 against produced 0292a021 addu s4,s4,s2. The 1-word state reproduces, so attempt 3's record stands and the work starts from it.

The pass that spoils the increment is named, from the pinned compiler's own -da streams (matchkit trace func_802149C0). Insn 233 is (set (reg 90) (plus (reg 90) (const_int 1))) and stays that way through rtl, jump, cse, loop, cse2, bp, flow, combine, sched and lreg; it is still (plus (reg s4) (const_int 1)) in the greg dump and has become (plus (reg s4) (reg s2)) by sched2. Nothing between greg and sched2 but reload, so the substitution is reload's post-reload constant-to-register pass, which records what each hard register holds, invalidates only call-clobbered registers at a call and clears every record at a CODE_LABEL. That is why the constant must be in a callee-saved register for the defect to appear and why a sentinel landing in v1 does not trigger it, and it is why -fno-thread-jumps cures the increment: the merge CODE_LABEL survives between the li and the increment and clears the record. Measured in the same streams: the merge label is code_label 219, alive in rtl, jump, cse and loop, gone by cse2, and in greg jump_insn 222's predecessor is call_insn 217 with no label between. Two jump_insns sit between the li and insn 233 in every stream, so this pass does not clear at a jump, only at a label. Also measured and failed: writing the call's result into the sentinel (i = func_8024E7CC(candidate);) leaves 1044 bytes and the same single word, because the dead set is removed before reload ever sees it.

The two words are complementary at the project's own -O2, not only under -fno-thread-jumps, and the permuter found the second spelling in 8 iterations. Comparing the store guard against a variable that holds zero rather than the literal (if (entry != (Actor *) none)) defeats the jump threader, because at threading time the comparison is register against register; cse then folds the variable to zero so the compare still assembles as beqz s0 and costs nothing. Traced: in that variant code_label 222, the merge before the guard, is alive in every stream from rtl through greg, and the increment stays (plus (reg s4) (const_int 1)) in greg and in sched2, so the byte at word 94 is right. The price is word 80: the surviving label is what the first null test branches to, so it assembles as 12000009 (beqz s0,0x80214B28) where the cartridge has 1200000e (beqz s0,0x80214B3C). Measured and failed on the other side: an explicit goto gathered on the null path with the opaque-zero guard kept (variant D) puts the first test back on 0x80214B3C, loses the label and returns the increment to addu s4,s4,s2, one word at 94; comparing both tests against the same zero variable (variant E) makes the variable live and costs 1048 bytes and 233 words. Zero-use labels are not a lever: a named C label placed immediately before the store guard (B) and immediately before func_8024E7CC (C) both leave 1044 bytes and the same single word, so this compiler deletes an unreferenced label before reload sees it.

Why this residue is not reachable from C at the project's stated -O2, as five measured steps rather than an opinion. One: the word at 94 is right only when reload's constant-to-register substitution is blocked, and that pass clears its record of what a hard register holds at a CODE_LABEL and, at a call, only for call-clobbered registers; the sentinel is in s2, callee-saved, so the call at 0x80214B20 does not clear it. Two: the only other way to break the record is an instruction that writes s2 between the li and the increment, and the cartridge has no such instruction in 0x80214B1C-0x80214B34, so that costs a word by construction. Three: the li must dominate the compare at 0x80214B18 and sits in the block that begins at the join label 0x80214B00, because delayed-branch scheduling fills the slot at 0x80214B10 only from that block; so a clearing label would have to fall in 0x80214B08-0x80214B38. Four: a CODE_LABEL survives to reload only with a use, measured twice - a named but unreferenced C label before the guard and before the call each changed nothing. Five: the cartridge's complete branch-target set for this interval is 0x80214A24, A30, A68, A90, AE0, B00, B3C, B5C, BB4, C08, C1C, C2C, CF8, D00, D34, D40, D4C and D94, and not one address lies in 0x80214B04-0x80214B38, so no surviving label can exist there. The two requirements therefore exclude each other: the label that fixes word 94 must be branched to, and every branch that could reach it is a word the cartridge spends elsewhere. The permuter agrees by its own blindness rather than by disagreeing: its scorer normalises branch targets, so both spellings score zero, and 31 zero-score outputs confirmed with try over about 10000 iterations every one landed on word 80 and none on 94. This is the whole story only for this instruction sequence; the residue would move only if some other control shape produced all 261 words differently, and 260 of them, including the three compare words the previous pass settled, are already exact.

The permuter sweep that produced attempt 4 is still running and bounded. It is artifacts/candidate-trials/permuter/sweep-func_802149C0.sh, started detached with --keep-going and eight jobs from artifacts/candidate-trials/permuter/input-func_802149C0/func_802149C0.c, which is attempt 3's draft; artifacts/candidate-trials/permuter/watchdog-func_802149C0.sh stops it forty minutes in. Progress is artifacts/candidate-trials/permuter/func_802149C0.sweep.log for the iteration counter and artifacts/candidate-trials/permuter/func_802149C0.confirm.jsonl for the answer, which carries one line per zero-score output with the full try verdict and would carry a line beginning MATCH if any output were byte-identical. Read it with tail, and count the words it is landing on with grep -o '"first_differing_word": [0-9]*' on that file. Note for whoever resumes: this sweep's tree is under [state].trials and is swept, so anything worth keeping from it goes through record-failure --candidate, which is how the second spelling became 4.c.

reload_cse_regs (reload1.c:7869, run whenever optimize > 0 at toplev.c:3501 with no flag of its own) was read in the rebuilt compiler source rather than inferred: it forgets a hard register value completely at a CODE_LABEL (reload1.c:7900-7908) and at a call only for the call_used_regs (reload1.c:7929-7937), never at a jump, since JUMP_INSN is rtx class i and CODE_LABEL is x (rtl.def:354, :372), and reload_as_needed applies the same two rules a second time (reload1.c:4207-4213, 4217-4223); 0x80214B04-0x80214B38 carries no label, so the remembered value persists across it and the two retained one-word spellings that exclude each other are both consistent with that record rather than one of them being a near miss the other fixes.

CORRECTION to observation 10, which framed this function as a question about how reload remembers what a hard register holds: that framing is wrong for this word. The single differing word is word 80 at 0x80214B00, expected 1200000e, produced 12000009, and it is a BRANCH DISPLACEMENT, not a register: cartridge beqz s0, 0x80214B3C against candidate beqz s0, 0x80214B28. All 260 other words are byte-identical including every register field. The cartridge compiler threaded that branch past the second, redundant beqz s0 at 0x80214B28 straight to 0x80214B3C and the candidate did not; both reach the same place. Measured with the new reload decision stream rather than inferred: reload made no decision anywhere in 0x80214B04 to 0x80214B38 (insns 189 to 241), the whole function has six reloaded insns at 381, 391, 423, 449, 485 and 551 and all are after the interval, s0 is reg 16 with 35 uses from pseudos and 0 penalty, it is never a spill register, and no pseudo loses reg 16 anywhere in the function. reload_cse belief in the interval records reg 2 holding the two lh sign-extends at insns 194 and 207, carries both across the jumps at 196 and 209 and drops reg 2 at the call at insn 220; it records nothing about s0 being zero, because reload_cse tracks what a register holds as an expression and never what a branch proved about it. So the reload facts in observation 10 remain true about the compiler and are simply not the cause here. The pass that decides this word is thread_jumps in jump.c, run as jump2, and it has no decision log, so the stream that would answer it does not exist yet. The route is therefore to make jump threading fire by removing the redundant second test from the control flow rather than to look for a register or a reload lever, and the two retained one-word spellings should be re-read with that in mind.

SUPERSEDES observation 11 on attribution, though not on the finding that the word is a branch displacement rather than a register. The pass is thread_jumps, but it is not part of jump2: thread_jumps is called twice directly from toplev.c, at :3286 with flag_before_loop=1 and at :3381 with flag_before_loop=0, both under flag_thread_jumps and both BEFORE register allocation. The jump2 pass at toplev.c:3641 is jump_optimize(insns, 1, 1, 0), cross-jumping and no-op deletion, and it never calls thread_jumps. Traced through the streams the prover already keeps, with no new instrumentation: insn 225 is the second beqz s0 at 0x80214B28, and it reads (eq (reg/v:SI 84) (reg/v:SI 95)) in .cse2, .flow, .combine and .sched, then (eq (reg/v:SI 84) (const_int 0)) in .lreg, then (eq (reg/v:SI 16 s0) (const_int 0)) in .greg and .jump2. b1 is jump_insn 185, (eq (reg 84) (const_int 0)) to label 222, and code_label 222 is immediately followed by insn 225. So at the time thread_jumps ran, both times, the first operands were identical at reg 84 while the second operands were (const_int 0) against (reg/v:SI 95), and rtx_equal_for_thread_p refuses on that. Pseudo 95 is substituted to zero only at local allocation, which runs after both thread_jumps calls, and jump threading never runs again. Therefore the lever is not reload, not register choice and not jump2: for the cartridge to have threaded, its second test must already have matched before thread_jumps, so the question is why cse_main did not collapse pseudo 95 to zero at that point, which is cse.c. The route for a candidate is a source shape where the second test is already the same expression as the first at cse time rather than one CSE only proves equal later. Instrumenting thread_jumps would print that the second operands differ and would add nothing, because the answer is already readable from .cse2 plus .lreg.

observations.note: Left retired after review against the compiler's attested idioms: the six-word residue is sine and negated cosine exchanged between two callee-saved float registers, and no attested idiom addresses which floating-point register a value is given. one-local-per-purpose covers merged live ranges taking a callee-saved register and its levers were already tried and recorded here, and shared-loop-counter-priority-is-not-a-lever is a negative result about integer counters and cursors. Reinstate when an idiom names floating-point register pairing.

Measured against the diagnostic compiler, not left as an open class. The galloc stream does report the float class: on 270 matched intervals that use the callee-saved float registers it ranked 954 FP_REGS allocnos beside 1500 in GR_REGS, with the same priority, conflict, could_hold, pass and took lines, so the earlier gap was in the reading and not in the instrumentation. What it shows is that the register a float value gets is its position in the allocation order and nothing else: in 88 of 95 of those intervals the callee-saved float registers were handed out in ascending order along the allocation order, and 1 of 321 such allocnos took a register it had stated a preference for. Of 226 adjacent pairs that both took a callee-saved float register, 214 were ordered by priority and only 12 by allocno number, which is the tie declaration order reaches, so the declaration-order attempts recorded above were working a lever that settles one pair in twenty. The decisions for this interval itself could not be read: no draft was retained for any of its ten attempts, and matchkit decisions needs a candidate to compile, so re-deriving one draft is the next step and not another spelling. No idiom was added, because a signal that fires on all 175 matched intervals with two or more float allocnos predicts nothing.

Compare structure, not word counts: attempt 3's file re-measured today is 1473 words, 140 hunks, 225 instructions, and the private sdiff.py those attempts scored with left part of every branch and jump target in its key, so its hunk counts carried displacement noise and are not comparable; matchkit structure and matchkit pool now do both readings in the toolkit. Fixed and confirmed against the cartridge. var_s0_8 and var_s1_5 are s32, not s16, which turns the draft's lhu into the cartridge's lh at 0x8021f90c and 0x80220258 and removes their sign-extension pairs; var_s1_3 must stay s16, because widening it as well is what produced attempt 3's 555-instruction fallout, and instead its three consumers read one s32 local assigned once before the *4, the / and the %, so the sll/sra pair appears once rather than per use. The two bar loops indexed the float tables four times too far: the draft carried var_s0 = 0x10 stepping 4 as an element index, while the cartridge's li s0,16 / addu at,at,s0 / addiu s0,s0,4 is a byte offset, that is elements 4 through 7; corrected to var_s0 = 4 stepping 1, which reads the words the cartridge reads and costs nothing structurally. A float comparison constant is a local, not a literal: var_floor = 0.0f assigned beside var_hud and compared as temp_f0 < var_floor is worth four hunks and seven instructions and leaves the pool exact. Ruled out. Rewriting the bar subscript as D_800CF1A8[i + 4] over a single induction variable regresses again, confirming the standing note; the pinned compiler makes no byte-offset giv either way and the cartridge's strength reduction is still unexplained. Testing the accumulation loop's back edge against arg0->field1338 instead of the decrementing local reaches exactly 7044 bytes and 1761 instructions but compiles to li a0,1 / bnez a0, an infinite loop; the cartridge does addiu a1,a1,-1 then slt v0,s0,a1, so the local is right and the byte count was coincidence. Hoisting arg1->0x2A4 into one local read once loads 676(s7) eleven times where the cartridge loads it thirteen, and is worse by words. Inlining the first bar loop's second product into the call argument reads 127 hunks over 205 instructions and 7048 bytes, which is better on every structural count, but only because the inlined subscript then falls after the loop's increment and reads the next element; sequenced correctly it is 130 over 208, worse than leaving the temporary alone. Blocking. The earliest structural divergence is unchanged and is register choice, not statement order: the cartridge loads pool slot 0 into $f0 and copies it to $f1 after both divides, and $f0 and $f1 already hold those divides' operands, so the anti-dependencies pin the pair where it is; the draft's allocator gives the pair $f2 and $f3, which are free, so the scheduler floats the load above the first divide and the copy into the middle. Every callee-saved float assignment is shifted by one from there (cartridge f23, f26, f24, f22, f21, f25 against draft f24, f25, f26, f22, f20, f21) and that shift is most of the remaining single-instruction hunks, so whatever forces the scratch pair at 0x8021eff8 should carry the rest. D_80110634 is the other named difference: the cartridge materialises its address once as lui v1,0x8011 / addiu v1,v1,1588 and then uses lw a0,0(v1) and sw v0,0(v1), while the draft emits lui/lw and lui/sw at both sites, the same instruction count in different bytes. The permuter is the instrument that moved this round: every win came from matchkit permute seeded on the current best and then re-derived by hand on the readable source, and its outputs must be read for meaning first, because two of its best-scoring candidates were semantically wrong. Second pass, same attempt. The base register for D_801468A0 is a second systematic defect, visible at every group: the cartridge materialises the plain symbol (lui s1,0x8014 / addiu s1,s1,26784 at 0x8021f03c, and again into s0 at 0x8021f9d4) and indexes it positively (lw v0,32(s1) at 0x8021f044 and 0x8021f08c; lw v0,152(s0) and lw v0,36(s0) at 0x8021f9dc and 0x8021fa38), while the draft folds the first access of each group into the base (la s0,D_801468A0+32 then lw v0,0(s0); la s0,D_801468A0+152 then lw v0,0(s0) and lw v0,-116(s0)). Same instruction count, different bytes, at five sites, and it also decides which callee-saved integer register the group occupies: the cartridge leaves s0 holding the D_8014687C base and takes s1, the draft clobbers s0. Reading the group through a local s32 * does not fix it. A pointer assigned just before the first group is constant-propagated straight back and the output is unchanged to the instruction; a pointer held across the middle group costs a callee-saved register and changes the frame, taking the candidate to 139 hunks over 229 instructions and moving the first divergence from instruction 72 back to 8; one held across the whole function makes the pinned compiler exit 33 with no error text at all, only its usual warnings, which is a register-pressure limit rather than a source fault. Also ruled out at the 0x8021eff8 divergence: it is not statement order. Swapping the two initialisers, the two multiplies, which variable each multiply consumes, or the two divides, moving the initialisers ahead of the divides, and swapping or relocating the two declarations all compile to the identical 129 hunks over 207 instructions; only moving the divides after the guard changes anything, and that is worse. A further 4,400-iteration search seeded on this candidate produced nothing better on the ordered criteria: its best by instruction count reaches exactly 1761 instructions but loses a literal use site, so its pool drifts to 0x800C76EC with two hunks, and its best by hunk span moves the first divergence earlier, to instruction 67. Read the first divergence as later-is-better; three candidates this round looked like gains until that was applied.

observations.note: Attempt-2 draft recovered and re-measured. The pre-retention draft the attempt-2 note names by its swept drafting directory survived in a retired copy of the workspace tree and re-measures today at exactly 9 differing words of 259, 1036 of 1036 bytes, with no unplaced literals. The 9 words are one transposition and nothing else: the pair 'sdc1 f21,0x80(sp); lwc1 f21,0x98(sp)' -- save the callee-saved float register, then load the fifth, stack-passed float argument into it -- sits at words 1 and 2 in the draft and at words 8 and 9 in the cartridge, after 'sw s3,0x6c(sp)' and before 'sw ra,0x70(sp)'. Word 0 and words 10 through 258 are byte-identical, so register allocation, frame layout and the whole body already agree; the residue is only where the prologue scheduler placed that one pair.

Prediction before measuring. func_8024FD4C is the matched sibling of this function: same job on a different record type, the same frame slots (0x60-0x6c for s0-s3, ra at 0x70, f20 at 0x78) and the same opening body, and its cartridge prologue orders the save/copy pairs strictly in parameter order, arg0 then arg1 then arg2 then arg3, with 'sw ra' and 'sdc1 f20' last. The cartridge prologue of func_8024F940 is that same order with the fifth, stack-passed float taking its turn after arg3. The one source-level difference between the matched sibling and this draft at the top of the body is that the sibling passes func_8024DD00 its four incoming parameters while this draft calls it with an empty argument list; in the sibling that call still assembles to a bare jal with no argument setup, because the values are already in a0-a3. Prediction: giving func_8024DD00 its four arguments and a real prototype keeps a0-a3 live into the call, changes the prologue block's dependence graph, and moves the 'sdc1 f21; lwc1 f21' pair from words 1-2 to words 8-9, reaching 0 differing words.

Prediction confirmed on the first measurement: byte-identical, 1036 of 1036 bytes, 0 differing words. The only change from the 9-word draft was giving func_8024DD00 a prototype of four parameters and passing it arg0 through arg3, exactly as the matched sibling func_8024FD4C does. The call still assembles to a bare jal with no argument setup because the values are already in a0-a3, so the change is invisible except in the prologue schedule: keeping a0-a3 live into the call reorders the block so the save-and-copy pairs come out in parameter order and the stack float's 'sdc1 f21; lwc1 f21' pair takes its turn after 'sw s3' instead of being hoisted to the top. Generalisable: when a near miss is confined to the prologue schedule and the first statement is a call, check whether that call should be carrying the incoming parameters.

Second measured fact, from rewriting the matching draft into typed C in the matched sibling's conventions. Naming the structures, giving the compact record its fields, passing the scale and position as f32 through the real prototypes of func_802734EC and func_802734B8, and inlining the colour-key step the way func_8024FD4C does all hold the match. One spelling does not: D_800D2B40 must be read as an array, 'extern s32 D_800D2B40[]' and D_800D2B40[0], not as the plain scalar that func_8024FD4C reads. The scalar form costs 5 words at word 149 and nothing else, because it lets the lui/lw pair for that load be scheduled ahead of the last 'swc1' of the fixed-cube maximum instead of after it. So the array spelling is load-bearing here and the scalar spelling is load-bearing in the sibling; the same symbol takes a different spelling in the two functions.

First, the gate is invoked through the project Makefile, which forwards each goal to 'decomp' found on PATH; a shell that can reach the toolkit only by absolute path gets 'decomp is not on PATH' from the Makefile, and the queue charges that to the function: attempt 3 here is recorded as failed with aligned_differing_words -1 against a candidate that was already byte-identical, so an environment fault spent one of the ten attempts. observations.note: Byte-identical in four measured trials from the blueprints, no permuter. Reuse path: func_80251754 gives the lock and the hash lookup (its goto spelling, with the asymmetric store forms, is what produces words 0-63 exactly); func_80252450 gives the lock/unlock inlines and, decisively, the Manager struct (queue 0x92C, pending 0x92C, active 0x940, lock 0x960) -- one struct object makes the compiler reach the lock queue from whichever base register is already live, which is why the same source spelling yields %hi/%lo(D_80105140) at one site, base+0x960 at another, base+0x34 at a third and base-0x14 at a fourth. Manager must be extended with a word at 0x99C (the symbol D_8010517C) so the active-list head is reached as -0x5C off that base; D_8010515C stays a separate extern because every reference to it rematerialises its address even with a Manager base live. Four measured facts that each cost a trial: (1) the refcount bump is an inline taking Node*, so its parameter load is killed by its own stores and re-derived afterwards -- writing found->node->count and found->node->flags inline instead reloads between the two and misses; (2) the stamp store and the func_80255F58 call share one node pointer, so they belong in a second inline over Node*, which puts the store in the call's delay slot; (3) the request fill order is key, priority, owner, tag, mode, node, extra -- store order to one base is preserved and only the tag store moves, into the delay slot of the following branch; (4) the async path must read 'if (found != 0) return found->node; return 0;' and not the inverted 'if (found == 0) return 0;' -- the inverted form lets the compiler cross-jump that return back into the hash-hit return and costs exactly one word. Frame 0x30, one spilled local at sp+0x10 reused for the looked-up request, the allocated one and the started one; s0=key (reused as the Manager base once key is dead), s1/s2 the two nodes, s3=arg9, s4=arg5; arg8 at 0x4C is never read.

observations.note: Left retired after review against the compiler's attested idioms: the six-word residue is the two stick floats exchanged between two caller-saved float registers, which is the same unexplained class as func_80215868 and func_8029D288, and no attested idiom addresses floating-point register pairing. Reinstate with those two when one does.

The three float residues are not one class, and this interval is the evidence. Its cartridge text has no call at all and saves no callee-saved float register, so the two stick floats contest the caller-saved bank with nothing crossing a call to constrain either; func_80215868 contests the callee-saved bank across eleven calls, and func_8029D288 exchanges a loaded limit against a materialised zero. The allocator is the same in all three and so is the rule -- position in the allocation order decides the register, measured on 270 matched intervals -- but that rule fires on every one of the 175 matched intervals with two or more float allocnos, so it names no lever and no idiom was added for it. What is specific here and worth the next attempt: on 125 matched intervals with float compares and moves but no call and no callee-saved float register, 85 still had two or more FP_REGS allocnos in galloc, so these two floats are almost certainly greg's and not local allocation's, and the lalloc stream will be silent about them however carefully it is read. The decisions could not be read for this interval: no draft was retained for any of its eleven attempts and matchkit decisions needs a candidate to compile.

attempts.note: One indivisible 1134-instruction function of 4536 bytes; no draft was compiled, so there is no word count. Verified against the cartridge: the two words the classifier reports before the frame allocation are an ordinary lui/lw of D_80110620 that the scheduler hoisted above the prologue, so the stray-before-prologue flag is not evidence of anything but scheduling and the interval is ordinary C. The body dispatches through a register at 0x8026A2B8 off three jump tables (0x800C96D8, 0x800C9708, 0x800C9738) and reads a literal pool of roughly thirty distinct slots spanning 0x800C96B0..0x800C9750 and 0x800D15C8..0x800D15F9, many of them paired as sym and sym+4 and two of them byte reads at 0x800D15F8 and 0x800D15F9. Because the compiler allocates one pool slot per use site in first-use order with no dedup by value, that whole ordering has to be reproduced before the instruction stream can be judged at all, and the unit lands only as a whole. Ruled out: nothing in the interval is retyped data or privileged; what blocks it is scale plus the pool ordering.

attempts.note: Read the global-allocation decision log before touching the source, and it changed what this residue is. The log (artifacts/drafts/func_8026CE18/trace/func_8026CE18.galloc, 1,948 lines, 26 allocnos) shows the draft already at maximum pressure: all nine callee-saved registers are taken and four allocnos are left in memory, and each of the four -- pseudo 81 player, 82 matrix, 84 lights, 86 pass -- reports 'could hold nothing in class GR_REGS at this point' with 'conflicts hard now' holding 16-23 and 30 where 'conflicts hard' at ranking time held none of them. By the record's own reading that is an order artefact, not a constraint, so the lever is the ranking. Every one of the twenty-five adjacent pairs in the allocation order is 'decided by priority' and none by allocno number, so the order is not reachable by moving declarations; refs and live_length are the only levers. The cartridge wants pass (priority 199: floor_log2(4) 2 * refs 4 / live_length 402) to hold s7 while player (338, refs 7 over 412) sits at 0x44(sp) and is reloaded at all five of its uses. The formula is monotone in refs at equal live_length, so no source form ranks a four-reference pseudo above a seven-reference one over the same span: pass would need eight references, and the cartridge's own code mentions it three times. That prediction was tested rather than assumed. Making the two memory-resident flags volatile, which is the only C spelling that takes a pseudo out of the competition, did free s6/s7/fp -- and the log shows player taking 23 and lights taking 30 while pass and matrix stayed in memory, exactly as the ranking says, for 274 words: pressure relief cannot reach pass. What did move the draft was writing lit and flashing as single assignments rather than a zero initialiser plus a conditional set: 273 to 259 aligned differing words, 1,072 of 1,124 bytes, with the flags' live_length falling from 206/205 to 175/183 and the memory-resident set unchanged. So the earlier note's framing -- a global-allocation priority search -- is refuted by the pass's own log: the disposition the cartridge has is not reachable from this reference structure, and the divergence is upstream of allocation. The next reader should look for what gives the cartridge one more long-lived competitor than this draft has: it materialises the address of D_80110634 three times (0x8026CFB0, 0x8026D020, 0x8026D0A0) and then copies it into s3 for the loop, where this draft holds one pseudo with 33 references in s0 across insns 210-637. loop-cost is silent here, and correctly so: the log records one loop, threshold 63 over insn_count 86, and zero givs, so no strength-reduction decision touches this function. Draft: artifacts/retained-candidates/func_8026CE18/3.c

observations.note: Pursued the recorded lead -- the cartridge materialises the address of D_80110634 three times and copies it into s3 for the loop -- and the loop pass's own dump settles half of it and refutes the other half. No attempt spent: the best draft is still attempt 3 at 259 aligned differing words, and nothing tried here beat it. The address half already reproduces. The retained stream artifacts/drafts/func_8026CE18/trace/source.i.loop records exactly one movable in the part loop: 'Insn 608: regno 200 (life 4), move-insn savings 1  moved to 672', and insn 672 in that same dump is (set (reg 200) (symbol_ref D_80110634)) sitting immediately after the loop guard jump_insn 667, which is the preheader. The draft emits that as 'move s5,s2' before the loop where the cartridge emits 'addu $19,$16,$0'; the hoist, the pseudo and its position all agree. The three materialisations are not a decision any pass logs: they are how far common subexpression elimination carried one address constant, and the draft carries it further, holding one pseudo with 33 references where the cartridge holds three shorter ones. That difference costs no instructions on its own. What the deficit actually is: aligning the two disassemblies on their ten shared call sites puts the 13 missing instructions at +2 in the prologue, +1, +4 across the lights region, +3, +1, +2, then -5 in the loop's emit and +5 in the tail. The one named, structural item in that list is the command word. The cartridge hoists 0xDE000000 into s4 in the preheader (lui s4,0xde00 at 0x8026d0dc, loop head 0x8026d0e4) and stores from it. The draft rematerialises it inside the loop (lui v0,0xde00 at insn 245 of 268, loop back-edge at 252), and in the RTL that is insn 620, (set (reg 202) (const_int -570425344)), standing between insns 617 and 622 inside the conditional the call at 604 guards. The loop dump names insn 620 only under 'possible biv, reg 202, const = -570425344' and never as a movable -- not moved, and not declined either, so the pass never considered it one, which is the difference from reg 200. Prediction and test: if the constant were a loop-invariant local set in the preheader, loop optimisation would have an insn there to keep. It does not survive. Declaring u32 tag = 0xDE000000 before the for loop and storing tag inside it measures 259 words and 1,072 bytes, identical to the draft without it, because constant propagation puts the constant back at its single use and recreates insn 620 in the same place. Reg 202 is read exactly once, at insn 622, so there is nothing for the pass to save by moving it. Conclusion on the lead, with the evidence above: at this optimisation level there is no C spelling of a single-use constant that reaches the loop pass as a movable, so the preheader copy the cartridge has is not source-reachable from this shape, and the remaining -5/+5 around the call is the delay-slot scheduler's, which this compiler writes no decision log for. Do not spend a further attempt re-searching either. What is still unexamined and is where the next attempt belongs: the +4 across the lights region and the +2 in the prologue, which no pass has been asked about yet.

The preserved four-word draft was also semantically wrong: it held the second flag mask in a variable declared char, so 0x1402 truncated to 0x02 and the function wrote flags or 2 where the cartridge writes flags or 0x1402. Widening that variable, or dropping it for the literal, corrects the value and keeps the distance at four words and the exact 628 bytes, so the earlier distance measured a draft that could not have been accepted. What remains is which of the two flag temporaries takes the first scratch register: the cartridge computes flags or 0x400 into the lower-numbered register and stores it first, keeping flags or 0x1402 alive across the intervening float store, and the pinned compiler makes the opposite choice. Swapping the two computations, naming both results as locals, and storing both expressions directly without locals all reproduce the same four words or regress to seven.

observations.note: Left retired after review against the compiler's attested idioms: the eight-word residue is a float register exchange between the unit limit and the zero constant, recorded across ten attempts with fifteen spellings and a nine-minute permuter run, and no attested idiom addresses floating-point register pairing. Reinstate with func_80215868 and func_80263E1C when one does.

Not the same residue as func_80215868, and the note pairing them should not be trusted. The cartridge text here saves one callee-saved float register and holds two unrelated values in it at different times, a vector length and then the polynomial result; the exchange recorded is between the loaded unit limit and the materialised zero, which are constants with very different live shapes, not two computed values competing for a pair of registers. Two things were measured. First, galloc does report FP_REGS -- 954 allocnos over 270 matched intervals, with priority, could_hold and took lines -- so this is readable and was not read; the decisions for this interval still could not be read, because no draft was retained for any of its ten attempts. Second, and this is the concrete next step: func_8029DAB4 is matched and contains the same clamp, polynomial and square-root block, and its source reads the limit through the named extern global, reaches the neighbouring slot as *(&D_800CAC38 + 1), writes every zero as a bare 0.0f literal, and uses the limit again afterwards in delta = D_800CAC38 - magnitude. That is a matched blueprint for exactly the block whose registers differ here, and it should be followed before any further spelling is tried.

observations.note: All three compiler facts drawn from this function were measured over the 3,725 matched intervals and all three were refused; do not spend a trial on any of them. (1) The claim that separate *K chains in the cartridge imply separate source statements has one witness in the whole tree (func_80403B70, factor 9) and zero witnesses for the folded counterpart the causal claim needs, and that single witness argues against it: a*36 + b*36 written across two statements compiled to (a*9 + b*9) << 2, so this compiler reassociates across a statement boundary and two separate chains do not prove two separate statements; the 187 to 111 movement was one trial in a 17-trial trajectory that also produced 184s, not a controlled measurement. (2) The loop counter is not a signal at all: a counter sits in a callee-saved register in 247 matched intervals and in a reloaded stack slot in 1, so the cartridge keeping it in a register is the universal default and this spill is a defect in the candidate rather than an idiom to key on; register pressure does not separate the one exception, which touches 6 callee-saved registers inside the range of the 247 that do not. So the route here is to relieve pressure until the counter stops spilling, not to look for a source shape that pins it. (3) Folding the advance into the argument register is the cartridge default at 513 sites in 259 intervals against 18 copy-shape sites in 14 intervals, and both proposed levers are contradicted: none of the 14 copy-shape intervals writes p += K then passes p, the one matched source that does write it folds instead (func_80407F6C), and 9 of the 18 copy sites never read the register again so multiple use does not explain it either. This interval is in the 3.4% minority shape with no rule behind it; read func_80240C9C, which holds both shapes in one byte-identical function, rather than reasoning from the population.

CORRECTION to observation 1, which refused the common-factor fact: that refusal was wrong and the fact is now attested by controlled compile, recorded as idiom common-factor-folds-in-one-expression. The compile used the build own command resolved from artifacts/us-rev1/description.mk, with the unmodified src/func_80403B70.c as a control whose .text came out byte-identical to the built object, so the command is the build and not an invented one. Same source, only the spelling of the sum changed: two statements (size = first->count * 36; then return size + second->count * 36 + 0x30;) gives two separate times-9 chains, while one expression (return first->count * 36 + second->count * 36 + 0x30;) forms the sum first and gives one chain, one word shorter. So two separate chains in the cartridge DO indicate the products were written in separate statements, and the 187 to 111 movement on this function is explained rather than coincidental. The boundary, which matters more than the rule: at a pure power of two both spellings fold, so a*16 + b*16 and s = a*16; s + b*16 differ only in the add operand order, and splitting statements is not a lever there and must not be tried. The chains survive separate statements only when the factor has an odd part greater than one, so check the factor at your site before spending a trial on this. What observation 1 got backwards: the times-4 hoisting in (a*9 + b*9) << 2 was read as proof the compiler reassociates across statements and therefore that two chains prove nothing; it is the opposite, the times-4 hoisting is the power-of-two half of the same rule and the times-9 staying split is the odd half. The population counts in observation 1 stand and are now the caveat rather than the refusal: the shape has 1 witness in 3725 matched intervals, 0 folded odd-factor counterparts anywhere, and 67 folded against 6 apparent-separate at power-of-two scale with all 6 read and none a sum of products. Observations on the loop counter and the pointer advance are unaffected and stay refused.

attempts.note: Re-drafted from the assembly, the prior eleven-word draft having been lost: 236 aligned differing words at 1,480 of 1,476 bytes, and the whole shape compiles and aligns instruction for instruction over most of the body. The galloc log was read before any source was written and answered a different question than the record asked. It does not show an s0/s1 swap, because this draft is not yet where the lost one was: ten allocnos get no register at all, the nine that win are all short-lived, and the longest-lived value that the cartridge keeps in a callee-saved register prices 1552 against 60000 for an allocno whose live_length is 5. The budget is the finding: the cartridge holds nine values in callee-saved registers and seven on the frame at 0x1DC to 0x1F4, so sixteen long-lived values, and this draft has nineteen. One prediction was tested and was wrong: routing all twelve bank accesses through one based object, which the cartridge does in the first-load block where it reaches the handle at -544 from its base register, cost 97 words and 20 bytes (236 to 333, 1480 to 1500). The cartridge reloads the bank table per region and shares a base only inside that one block, so the next pass keeps this draft's per-region reloads and bases only the handle, the name, the mapped address and the bank table of the first-load block together.

attempts.measured_by: re-measured with the aligner on us-rev1 from artifacts/retained-candidates/func_80410FD4/4.c
attempts.note: Resumed the retained attempt-3 draft at 236 aligned differing words and 1,480 of 1,476 bytes and took it to 174 words at 1,464 bytes with six measured source changes and five recorded failures; the budget premise the last record left was wrong, because the draft and the cartridge already agree on frame size 0x220, on the same nine callee-saved registers at 0x1F8-0x21C and on exactly the same eight frame slots 0x1D8-0x1F4, so both hold sixteen long-lived values and the whole residue is which value goes where. What worked: spilled locals take frame slots in declaration order ascending, so declaring texture, into, image, kind, tile, slot, threshold in that order lands them where the cartridge has them (236 to 230); the twelfth argument of func_804137A0 is listsByPass[pass] and not listsByPass[pass][0], one indirection not two (to 227 at 1,472); the byte count at the last func_804137A0 is * code >> 3 where the loop's sizes[i] is * code / 8, the cartridge emitting a bare sra there with no bltzl-addiu-7 rounding, which also lets the tile->wid and tile->siz loads be shared with the argument list (to 217 at 1,464); the bank table lookup written before the tile index is narrowed, because prologue saves come out in order of first definition (to 205); the first-load block reaching the file state through a File struct whose Tables sub-struct sits at 0x220, which is the base the cartridge shares for the handle at -544, the name at -540, the mapped base at +592 off the handle and the bank table at +88 (to 197), and then reaching banks through a Tables * while the mapped base stays a direct D_801539B0.tables.base member chain, which is the exact split the lost eleven-word draft's note described and which makes the whole first-load block align word for word (to 190); and dropping the bank local from the loaded test so it reads D_80153C28[group].loaded and bank is assigned only inside the block, matching the cartridge's temporary for the test and s5 inside (to 174). What failed: reaching D_801539B0 through a block-scoped s32 *handle at the release site produced a byte-identical object, so that shared base is not reachable from source; declaring the bank table volatile to force the cartridge's twelve reloads gave 333 words at 1,496; routing every bank access through the File object, not only the first-load block, gave 225 at 1,488, confirming attempt 3's result at a finer grain; dropping the bank local from the cached path too gave 184; and writing the cached-path test through slots[index] so that &slots[index] is a temporary, which is what would put the slot pointer in s1 the way the cartridge has it, gave 326 the first time and 314 again after the other six changes, so it is firmly not the mechanism. What is left is one cluster and one cause. The cluster is the entry and cached-path block, words 10 to 79: the cartridge puts the scaled group offset in s2, the pass slot table in s3 and the slot pointer in s1, and uses a0 as a temporary for the cached path's bank, where this draft puts the group offset in s1, the table in s2, spills the slot pointer to 0x1F0 at its definition and reloads it three times, and holds the cached-path bank in s5. Give the slot pointer a callee-saved register and the rest of the numbering follows. The cause of the remaining twelve bytes is that the cartridge materialises D_80153C28 twice inside each of the two func_804137A0 argument lists, once for offsets[...] and again for listsByPass[pass], where this draft common-subexpression-eliminates them into one; the cartridge loads that table twelve times and this draft nine, and no source spelling tried here reproduces the split.

observations.note: Attempt 4, first finding: the sixteen-versus-nineteen budget the attempt-3 record asked the next pass to work is already met. Disassembling the retained draft (artifacts/retained-candidates/func_80410FD4/3.c, re-trialled at 236 differing words, 1480 of 1476 bytes) beside the cartridge shows both use frame size 0x220, both save exactly ra plus nine callee-saved registers at 0x1F8-0x21C (s0,s1,s2,s3,s4,s5,s6,s7,fp), and both touch exactly the same frame slots: the outgoing argument area 0x10-0x30, the u8 first-argument home at 0x1D8, and seven 4-byte locals at 0x1DC,0x1E0,0x1E4,0x1E8,0x1EC,0x1F0,0x1F4. The slot sets are byte-for-byte the same list. So the draft holds sixteen long-lived values, not nineteen: the attempt-3 galloc reading counted allocnos, not the frame the compiler actually emitted, and the residue is not a pressure overage. What differs is which value goes where. The cartridge puts group*0x49C in s2 and the pass slot table in s3 and keeps the slot pointer in s1; the draft puts group*0x49C in s1, the slot table in s2, and spills the slot pointer to 0x1DC, reading it back. The cartridge also orders the prologue with the group scaling and the D_80153C28 load first and the which masking after, where the draft masks which first. Next lever is statement order in the entry block, not fewer live values.

Attempt 4, second finding, two measured wins on the retained draft (baseline 236 words / 1,480 bytes). (1) This compiler assigns frame slots to spilled locals in SOURCE DECLARATION ORDER, ascending. The draft's slots 0x1DC..0x1F4 held slot,tile,image,texture,into,kind,threshold, which is exactly its declaration order; the cartridge's hold texture,into,image,kind,tile,slot,threshold. Reordering the declaration block to that order and leaving the never-spilled locals after it: 236 to 230 differing words, no size change. The same rule puts sizes[0x60] at sp+0x38 and the 0x20-byte scratch texture at sp+0x1B8 in both, so aggregates obey it too. (2) The twelfth argument of func_804137A0 is listsByPass[pass], the list pointer, not listsByPass[pass][0]: the cartridge has one lw at each of the two call sites where the draft has two. Declaring the parameter s32 * and dropping the [0]: 236 to 233 and 1,480 to 1,472 bytes. The two are additive: together 227 differing words at 1,472 bytes, the best measured state of this function since the lost eleven-word draft. At 1,472 the draft is now one word SHORT of the cartridge's 1,476, and the missing word is in the entry block: the cartridge computes the bank pointer and the tile address by two separate addu chains from D_80153C28 (move v1,a0 then addu v1,v1,s2 then addu v1,v1,v0, plus addu a0,s2,a0), where the draft common-subexpression-eliminates them into one. The draft also still spills the slot pointer immediately after computing it and reloads it three times, where the cartridge holds it in s1 and spills it once, later, at the point it loads the bank image.

Attempt 4, third finding. Two more predictions measured on top of the declaration-order and list-pointer fixes (227 words / 1,472 bytes). PASSED: the byte count handed to the final func_804137A0 call is an arithmetic shift, not a signed division. The cartridge emits a bare sra v0,t0,3 there with no bltzl/addiu-7 rounding, while the loop's own sizes[i] computation twenty instructions earlier DOES carry the rounding, so the two are written differently in the source: the loop is * code / 8 and the tail call is * code >> 3. Making that one change: 227 to 217 differing words and 1,472 to 1,464 bytes, and it also let the compiler share the tile->wid and tile->siz loads between the argument list and the byte count, which is where most of the ten words came from (the cartridge has four lb off the tile there, the draft had six). FAILED, and worth not repeating: reaching D_801539B0 through a block-scoped s32 *handle at the release site, to reproduce the cartridge's lui/addiu/lw-0(s0)/sw-zero-0(s0) shared base, produced a byte-for-byte identical object to not doing it (227 words, 1,472 bytes, same comparison). The compiler folds *(&D_801539B0) straight back to the %hi/%lo pair, so that shared base is not reachable from source by a pointer local; it is an address-selection decision inside the compiler. Current best: 217 aligned differing words at 1,464 of 1,476 bytes, now three words short rather than one over.

attempts.note: Boundary, not C: classify reports func_80414D4C entered mid-interval at 0x804158B8 from func_80414428, but the 8 bytes at 0x80414428 (ROM 0x182428) are filler, not a function. Nothing in the tree references func_80414428; its two words 0x0810562E 0x02403821 are a verbatim copy of ROM 0x183428, and in the us cartridge the same gap (ROM 0x178428) holds ASCII 'OUND' plus 0x65717582, while the gap at ROM 0x1823D8 holds 0x8C50FFFC 0x06400014 here and 0x66000000 0x04000000 in us: stale bytes between functions that only decode as a jump here by coincidence. The repair cannot be made in the split: func_80414404 is already landed C, so ld emits obj/src/func_80414404.o for 0x182404-0x182428 only, and both deleting the 0x182428 interval and retyping it 'bin' drop those 8 bytes out of .text, shifting everything after and failing ASSERT(ABSOLUTE(.) == 0x8041B63C, 'text-alignment: func_8041B63C start'). Both variants were built and reverted; the tree reproduces the cartridge. Needs a split mechanism that keeps inter-function filler in .text without declaring it a function. This is a routing defect rather than a function defect: classify routes func_80414D4C to 'boundary' on the strength of the entry from func_80414428, but the boundary route has no move for an interval of this shape, where the offending interval is pure filler and the interval before it (func_80414404, ROM 0x182404) is already landed C. classify should recognise filler-behind-landed-C and stop routing the entered function to boundary. Two whole-file reverts of versions/us-rev1/ragewars.yaml were made while testing the two split variants; each was rebuilt and the tree reproduces the cartridge.

observations.note: Four measured compiler facts got this from 286 differing words of 322 to zero in one edit, and all four were established with probe compiles rather than guessed. (1) The compiler materialises a global's address biased by the offset of its FIRST use in the region, then reaches every later use of the same symbol as a signed offset from that register: a probe writing D_801462C8[0x1D] before &D_801462C8[0xD0] emitted addiu v1,v1,0x1D then addiu a0,v1,0xB3. It does NOT share a base across two symbols; D_801468A0 and D_801462C8 each got their own lui/addiu. The cartridge holds 0x801468A0 in s0 across the first call and reaches the word at +0xA8, the byte at -0x5BB and the slot array at -0x508 from it, so a single u8* base with those offsets is what reproduces it, not three flat symbols. (2) Two byte stores at different offsets of one 0x96-stride element share a single multiply only when the index is a named local: k = i * 0x96; p[k+0x78] = 0; p[k+0x91] = 0 gives one multiply and addu v0,v0,a0, while slot = &slots[i] gives one multiply but addu v0,a0,v0 and slots[i].field gives the right addu with the multiply duplicated. Only the named-index form gives both. (3) Passing &i to a call spills i and defeats strength reduction, which is what reproduces the reload-and-remultiply in all three loops; one local served every loop counter and the func_8041DBA0 out-parameter, which is why the frame has exactly one slot at 0x10(sp). (4) Deriving base+0x83 from the same symbol (&D_80102B00[i][0x83]) is what emits addiu s1,s0,0x83; a flat D_80102B83 costs a second lui/addiu pair. Naming a fresh local for the 0x43 panel rather than reusing the switch's handle avoided a move copy. Blueprint: src/func_8042E080.c gave the 0x96-stride slot layout and the D_801462C8/D_801468A0 pair, src/func_8041FF9C.c the D_80102B0D[i*0x190] flat-symbol idiom, src/func_80422728.c the screen-state shape.

observations.note: Held pending a named mechanism, not abandoned. Two aligned differing words at nine of ten attempts spent: the residue is the order of a hoisted constant copy and a pointer add before a call, and 27,275 permuter iterations plus every placement of the counter and pointer initialisers are recorded here as holding at two. Re-deriving a draft already known to sit at two words would spend the last attempt on a measurement the record already has, and destroy the attempt a future mechanism would need. Pick this up when an idiom names the ordering of a hoisted constant copy against an address add across a call, then reinstate it; do not pick it up to try harder.

The last attempt stays unspent, and now for a reason the compiler's own support states rather than for caution. The recorded residue is an ordering: the hoisted constant copy (move s2,v1) against the slot-pointer add before the call. The diagnostic build of the pinned compiler patches four compiler files -- global.c, local-alloc.c, loop.c and toplev.c -- and describes exactly three readable passes, global-alloc, local-alloc and loop-cost, which decide respectively which hard register a cross-block pseudo gets, which one a pseudo living inside a block gets, and whether an induction variable is strength-reduced and which giv absorbs which. None of the three decides where an instruction sits. The loop.c instrumentation is strength reduction only: every line it adds is a giv, a benefit, a threshold, a worth-while comparison or a combine_givs pairing, and nothing in it touches invariant hoisting's placement. Instruction order belongs to the scheduler, and the compiler's own trace record says so outright: GCC 2.8.1 has no -fsched-verbose, and the sched and sched2 streams carry the scheduled RTL, which is the result rather than the decision log. So the pass that owns these two words writes no log in this compiler, and no reading of the three that do can name the mechanism. A second, independent reason: the draft that reached two words is not on disk. Attempt 9 names a path under a drafting tree that no longer exists, and this cartridge has no retained candidate for this function, so even a pass that did own the decision could not be asked about the two-word draft without re-deriving it, which is the expenditure the cap exists to prevent. Pick this up when the diagnostic build gains a scheduler log, or when an attested idiom names the ordering of a hoisted constant copy against an address add across a call. Do not pick it up to try harder.

A loss, recorded here so nobody plans against a draft that does not exist. The two-word draft is unrecoverable. Attempt 9 recorded its path under a drafting tree that is swept, this cartridge keeps no retained candidate for this function, and the mechanism that retains a failed attempt's source shipped after that attempt was made. What was lost with it is 27,275 permuter iterations of search. Everything now known about the residue is a description taken from the cartridge's own assembly and from the attempt notes above: two aligned differing words, the order of a hoisted constant copy against the slot-pointer add before the call. Nobody can reread the draft, diff it, or run the diagnostic compiler's decision logs against it, so a tenth attempt would begin by re-deriving a two-word draft from the assembly and would spend the last attempt on a measurement this record already holds. Anyone picking this up starts from the assembly, not from a file.

attempts.note: Interval is one unit of five functions (func_8044CBE0, func_8044CD58, func_8044D024, func_8044D408, func_8044D9DC), about 1050 instructions, and it only lands when all five are byte-exact together; no draft was compiled, so there is no word count. Read against the cartridge: func_8044CBE0 is a teardown that calls func_802537D8(0, x) on eleven fields of arg0 (0x100, 0xB8, 0xBC, 0xC0, 0xC4, 0xC8, 0xD0, 0xD4, 0xEC, 0xCC, 0xE8), then three more each guarded by a null test (0xF0, 0xF4, 0xFC), then walks the list at arg0+0x1B500 unlinking through func_80255E78 and finishes with func_80254784 on the saved head; 0x1B500 is past the 16-bit displacement range, so it appears as lui 0x2 / addu / lw -0x4B00 for the load and as a hoisted 0x1B500 constant in a register for the address-of inside the loop. func_8044CD58 and func_8044D024 both repeat a six-call chain through func_8028FD94 and func_8028FDD8 ending in a bit test (1 shifted left by index&7, byte index sra(index+7,3) when the index is negative) against a byte table, and both write flag bytes at 0xE and 0xF of a 0x14-stride record. func_8044D024 spills nine values into its 0x68-byte frame at 0x18..0x38; func_8044D408 uses a 0x120-byte frame, recomputes the 0x2E8 element stride as ((n*3)<<5 - n*3)<<3, and carries a five-slot literal pool (D_800CA2E4, D_800CA2E8, D_800CA2E8+4, D_800CA2F0, D_800CA2F4) whose first-use order must be reproduced, plus the file-scope tables D_80145040/44/48, D_80145100/04/20 and D_80146398. Nothing in the unit looked non-C; what blocks it is size, and specifically that the two large functions are dominated by stack-slot assignment and spill ordering that only converge by iteration.

attempts.note: Second attempt: a complete compiling five-function draft now reaches .text 80.4486% on objdiff (matchkit structure), from 78.4362% at first draft; 889 of 1050 words still differ positionally because length shifts break alignment, so the section share is the honest figure. Draft kept at artifacts/drafts/func_8044CBE0.c. Solved and verified byte-exact against the cartridge: func_8044CBE0 itself, all 94 words, first try; and the unit's whole .rdata, five slots at 0x800CA2E4 holding FLT_MAX, pi, 204.8, -pi and 32768/pi, reproduced by one file-scope static const f32[5] read by index, which also fixes the section's 4-byte alignment that a bare float literal cannot. Three source-level idioms found: a statement whose value is only needed inside the guarded block must be written inside it, not before it (moving step = 0x1200 inside the func_80285150 guard moved it into the beqz delay slot and freed a callee-saved register); the cartridge keeps a raw count and a separate limit as two variables where a single decremented variable is tempting (func_8044D9DC holds the column count at sp+0x2C for the row stride and count-1 at sp+0x34 for the test, worth +1.6% on its own); and the literal at 0x800CA2EC is 434CCCCC, one ulp below 204.8f, so it must be written 204.79999f because this cc1 rounds rather than truncates decimal to float. Ruled out by measurement: the loop-counter initialiser placement canonicalises, all three positions give identical code; and hoisting the turn limit to a local made the clamp worse, 80.4486 to 80.3295, because the cartridge's pi lives in callee-saved f20 across the loop and an explicit local defeats that. What blocks the remaining four functions is register allocation and spill-slot layout, with no single knob: func_8044D024 wants MORE pressure than the draft produces, since the cartridge spills both parameters to their home slots at sp+0x68 and sp+0x6C and carries six further spill slots at sp+0x24..0x38 against a frame 8 bytes larger than the draft's, while func_8044D9DC wants LESS, since the cartridge keeps arg0 in s8 where the draft spills it to sp+0x68 and reloads it twice. Those pull in opposite directions within one object, so they cannot both be fixed by trimming or adding locals globally.
attempts.unmeasurable: no draft was retained for this attempt

attempts.note: Third attempt: .text 80.6771% on objdiff, from 80.4486% at the start of this pass and 78.4362% at first draft; aligned instruction counts per function are 94/94, 92/179, 110/249, 155/373, 70/153. Draft at artifacts/drafts/func_8044CBE0.c. Correcting my own attempt-2 note: reading the five float constants through a file-scope static const f32[5] was the WRONG call. It reproduced .rdata but cost the text, exactly as the float-constants-as-literals idiom predicts. Written as plain literals instead, the compiler saves f20 in the prologue with sdc1, holds pi across the loop and reuses it for the clamp's first and third comparison, and gives func_8044D408 a 288-byte frame with both parameter home slots at sp+0x120 and sp+0x124, all three matching the cartridge where the array version matched none of them; and the emitted .rdata comes out in the cartridge's own slot order, FLT_MAX first, with no array needed. That resolves the slot-order puzzle the attempt-2 note left open. Two further idioms established here. First, bgez then addiu 7 then sra is signed division by 8, not a shift: the bit index must be a signed int so the compiler cannot prove it non-negative, because declaring it u8 lets it fold to a single srl and drops three instructions the cartridge has; worth 92 aligned instructions in func_8044CD58 where 91 was the ceiling before. Second, a guard of the form slt limit, counter is what the compiler synthesises from a plain for loop, whereas an explicit if (limit >= 0) around a do/while folds to bltz against zero, a different instruction; func_8044D9DC's inner loop needs the for. One counter-example worth recording against the existing index-form-loop idiom, which is attested by func_8044E3E4 only: applying it to func_8044D408's spawn pointer cost 0.7%, because that loop genuinely walks the pointer in the cartridge and the rebasing there comes from the pointer being register-resident rather than spilled. The idiom is real but not universal, and the signal that distinguishes the two cases is whether the cartridge reloads the pointer from a stack slot each iteration. Remaining gap is still register allocation and spill placement; per-function and independent, as the coordinator established, not coupled across the object as attempt 2 wrongly claimed.

attempts.note: Fourth attempt: .text 81.2886%, from 80.6771%; aligned per function 94/94, 96/179, 107/249, 160/373, 73/153. Draft at artifacts/drafts/func_8044CBE0.c. One new idiom established, the strongest lever found so far: reusing a single local for two semantically distinct purposes merges their live ranges, so the compiler gives the merged variable a callee-saved register and evicts something that belongs there. Splitting them into separate short-lived locals matches the cartridge. It carries a discriminator, because the inverse is equally true and costs more than the fix gains. Split when the two uses differ in starting value or meaning: func_8044D408's nearest-neighbour loop starts from arg0->unk13C rather than zero and walks a second instance pointer, and giving it its own counters and pointer moved that body from 153 to 160 aligned instructions and the object from 80.82 to 81.26 percent; func_8044D9DC reused one local for the func_8028FE1C result and for the two func_80250754 and func_8024F6DC results, and splitting those moved it from 70 to 75; func_8044CD58 reused one local for the set object and the byte pointer derived from it, worth 92 to 96. Do NOT split when both uses start from the same value and the cartridge demonstrably reuses one register: func_8044D408's fill loop and its main loop both count from zero and share the cartridge's register, and splitting them cost 1.9 percent, from 81.26 down to 79.37. The signal to read before deciding is whether the cartridge's two loops increment the same register or different ones. Separately, the permuter is not the tool for this interval: 2000 iterations at --jobs 2 moved the score from 95600 to 95295 and never fell below 19 wrong instructions, because the search is over a 1050-instruction five-body object and the remaining faults are structural rather than local. Remaining gap is still register allocation and spill placement, worked per function as established.

attempts.note: Re-measured on the tree restored at 5b65dd1 after a full build under the landing lock; the four pinned binaries verify against decomp/sn64/toolchain.sha256 and the rebuilt image is cartridge us-rev1. .text 89.2238 percent, from 88.0981: func_8044CBE0 100, func_8044CD58 88.3296 (from 82.0615), func_8044D024 99.1165 (from 98.8755), func_8044D408 82.9598, func_8044D9DC 82.9032. Three source changes, each traced from the compiler's own intermediate streams before it was made rather than inferred from the emitted bytes. (1) Signed division by eight: write the bias out instead of dividing, t = i; if (t < 0) { t += 7; } then bits[t >> 3] and f(t, bits), in place of bits[i / 8] and f(i, bits). The greg stream says why the division form cannot match: the divisor expansion's temporary is pseudo 151, defined at insn 389 (the copy) and insn 393 (the plus-7 bias) and given hard register 4 (a0), while the index is pseudo 107 in 19 (s3), so the argument copy at insn 429 is a real move and not the no-op that insn 431's a1 copy became and lost for free. No C name reaches that temporary, so nothing can share it; written out it is an ordinary local and one local serves as dividend, shifted value and call argument. The whole division-and-call region of func_8044D024 is now identical and the jal to func_80245788 carries the cartridge's nop, confirmed in the dbr stream, which holds no sequence for that call at all. It is only correct because the index cannot be negative, which is what the cartridge's own code relies on. Recorded as the idiom signed-division-bias-written-out. (2) A struct field read inline as an argument to a chain of calls is a local in the cartridge: idx = arg0->unk1B40C before the chain and idx inside it, worth func_8044CD58 84.7709 to 87.6201, and it closed an exact two-instruction shortfall over two sites. (3) A cursor shared between two loops is split and a counter shared between them is not: splitting both gave 88.1899, the cursor alone 88.3296. Measured and rejected, so do not retry these without a new reason: the bias taken before the mask rather than after (88.6171 to 87.3695); the loop-head pointers advanced in place with the pool counts read first (88.6191); a second name for the context parameter across the two counting loops (89.0619); the priming loop's counter given a local of its own (89.0838). Five zero-cost constructs were measured against the division site and every one left the bytes unchanged at 88.2171 with the delay slot still filled: a self-assignment of the index before the call, three chained empty tests before it, a redundant copy of the index passed in its place, one local as dividend and mask source and argument at once, and that copy made before the mask. The empty-statement family does nothing on this compiler, so the earlier note's claim that the argument-register form of the division temporary could not be reproduced is withdrawn: it was reproduced, by removing the temporary from the allocator's reach rather than by steering the allocator.
